source_issues.title: GenerativeModelStore: _last_fetch_id can regress and defeat incremental fetch
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with full reproduction walkthrough: _last_fetch_id is updated to max id of delta batch on each poll, not a monotonic high-water mark. When an incremental fetch returns rows whose max id is lower than the previously-seen max, the cursor regresses and the next poll re-fetches everything between the new smaller cursor and the true global max. Impact: defeats the daemon's egress-savings purpose in cloud environments, causing increased DB read costs.

signals.topic: GenerativeModelStore daemon cursor regression causes unnecessary full re-fetch of model data
signals.summary: The GenerativeModelStore daemon's _last_fetch_id cursor can regress when an incremental fetch's max ID is lower than the prior high-water mark, causing the next poll to re-fetch all records between the regressed cursor and the true global max. This silently defeats the daemon's documented purpose of reducing DB egress in cloud environments.
signals.review_reason: This is a real functional bug with measurable cost impact. The daemon is designed to reduce DB egress (cloud cost savings), but the cursor regression bug silently causes full re-fetches on every delta where the max id is below the prior high-water mark. No data loss occurs (merge is idempotent), but the cost-optimization intent of the daemon is defeated. The bug is well-evidenced with a detailed reproduction walkthrough and code-level analysis.

source_issues.title: GenerativeModelStore: _last_fetch_id can regress and defeat incremental fetch
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with full reproduction walkthrough: _last_fetch_id is updated to max id of delta batch on each poll, not a monotonic high-water mark. When an incremental fetch returns rows whose max id is lower than the previously-seen max, the cursor regresses and the next poll re-fetches everything between the new smaller cursor and the true global max. Impact: defeats the daemon's egress-savings purpose in cloud environments, causing increased DB read costs.

signals.topic: Scheduler HTTP calls fail with 401 Unauthorized in multi-replica/multi-worker deployments due to per-process token generation
signals.summary: Each process generates a different internal_service_token at startup, causing 401 errors across replicas
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking in production multi-replica deployments. Scheduler silently fails with 401 Unauthorized, meaning jobs scheduled across replicas never complete. All three official deployment templates (Railway, AWS, Docker) are affected by default.

source_issues.title: fix(scheduler): internal_service_token not stable across replicas/workers
source_issues.evidence: When running with multiple replicas (Railway default: 2) or workers (AWS: 2), scheduler HTTP calls fail with 401 Unauthorized because each process generates a different internal_service_token at startup. The token is stored only in process-local memory. All three platform templates (Railway, AWS, Docker) enable scheduler=True but do not configure the token, causing silent production failures.

acontinue_run nested team no final message

source_issues.title: [Bug] Workflow cancellation is ineffective during continue run

signals.topic: permission.ask plugin hook silently dropped during Effect refactor, breaking all plugins that auto-allow commands

Plugin authors who registered permission.ask handlers to auto-allow read-only commands now have handlers that silently do nothing at runtime. signals.topic: Prompt caching bills 1.25x for unintended cache writes past explicit breakpoint — direct financial loss
signals.summary: When using explicit `cache_control` breakpoint (no top-level automatic caching opt-in), the server writes additional cache entries past the breakpoint in warm calls. These writes are billed at 1.25x cache-write rate but never read back, causing direct financial loss with no documented opt-out mechanism.
signals.review_reason: User is directly billed at 1.25x rate for tokens that are never read back — confirmed financial loss with a reproducible script. This is a core API billing mechanism bug, not an edge case. The user cannot prevent the extra charges as there is no documented opt-out. Issue is open, recently active, and reproduces consistently.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Server writes additional cache entries past explicit `cache_control` breakpoint, billing 1.25x for tokens that are never read
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction script shows warm calls writing ~1416 extra tokens at 1.25x rate (cache_creation=1416 on Call 2 & 3) that are never read back (cache_read only ever reads the 2227 tokens from the original breakpoint). User reports confirmed across SDK versions 0.79.0–0.102.0. No documented way to opt out. Financial cost loss confirmed with actual token counts.

signals.topic: Tool runner infinite loop when append_messages() is called inside the iteration loop — main agent workflow blocked
signals.summary: Calling runner.append_messages() inside the tool runner for-loop sets _messages_modified=True, which skips auto-append of the assistant message and tool result. The next iteration sends a request with no tool result in history, causing Claude to re-issue the same tool call indefinitely. The issue is in the official advanced usage documentation example.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocking bug in the agent tool runner — the official advanced usage example causes an infinite loop, completely blocking any agent workflow that tries to append messages mid-loop. Root cause is identified in SDK source code. The issue is not an edge case but a fundamental interaction between append_messages and the runner's auto-append mechanism, and the broken pattern is directly from official documentation.

source_issues.title: [Bug] append_messages() inside tool runner loop causes infinite loop (advanced usage docs example)
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified in _beta_runner.py line 281: _messages_modified=True skips auto-append of tool result, causing infinite re-execution of the same tool call. Minimal reproduction provided. The problematic pattern is directly from the official 'Advanced usage' documentation page. The correct pattern (from 'Modifying tool results' example) is inconsistent with the broken one.

signals.topic: files.beta.upload mutates input dict/tuple in-place via deepcopy_minimal — silent state corruption
signals.summary: deepcopy_minimal recursively copies lists and dicts but stops at tuples, leaving nested Mapping objects (e.g., HTTP headers dict) mutated in-place after the upload call. The caller's original data structure is silently corrupted with no error or warning.
aliases: input parameter mutated after API call
signals.review_reason: Silent in-place mutation of caller's data structures is a serious state corruption issue. The bug can corrupt application state without raising any error, making it hard to debug. Users may not notice the corruption until downstream code fails in non-obvious ways. Affects a core API operation (file uploads) and the same pattern may exist in other deepcopy_minimal call sites. 6 comments confirm other users have hit this.

source_issues.title: Use of `deepcopy_minimal` in `files.beta.upload` mutates dict in place
source_issues.evidence: User empirically verified that the 'headers' dict inside the File tuple parameter is modified in-place after calling files.beta.upload(). Screenshots show the before/after state of the dict. Bug traced to deepcopy_minimal at src/anthropic/_utils/_utils.py#L187 which does not recurse into tuples. 6 comments confirm the issue, indicating other users have encountered it.

signals.topic: Token counting API errors on Bedrock — key feature unavailable on major deployment platform

signals.topic: Message batch custom_id character limit undocumented — causes opaque 400 BadRequest errors

aliases: batch API parameter validation not documented
signals.review_reason: Undocumented parameter constraint causes opaque 400 errors for batch API users. While not financially costly, it causes repeated trial-and-error and blocks batch workflow setup. 3 comments confirm multiple users have hit this. The fix (adding the constraint to SDK validation and/or documentation) is straightforward but the issue has been open since June 2025 without resolution.

source_issues.title: Message Batch Processing - undocumented character limit for custom_id parameter

signals.topic: Bundled Claude binary hangs indefinitely in non-TTY environments (CI, Docker, cron, launchd)
signals.summary: The bundled Claude Code CLI checks isatty() on stdout and hangs forever when stdout is a pipe or file. This completely blocks the main query() flow in CI pipelines, Docker containers without -t, cron jobs, and launchd agents. No output, no error, just silent hang. Combined with RateLimitEvent stream hangs, pipelines time out at 1800s+ repeatedly.
signals.review_reason: Main flow completely blocked in non-interactive deployments — CI, Docker, cron, launchd. Silent hang with no error, no progress, indefinite timeout. Affects the dominant SDK deployment shapes (orchestrators, headless servers, containerized workers). Clear user impact with documented production pipeline failures.

source_issues.title: Bundled `claude` binary hangs when stdout is not a TTY (pipe / file / launchd / cron / Docker)

signals.topic: Premature TaskNotificationMessage causes cascading orchestrator failures in parallel subagent dispatch
signals.summary: TaskNotificationMessage fires to the orchestrator while the subagent is still mid-execution (76-850s remaining), causing the orchestrator to misinterpret an incomplete subagent as done. This cascades into incorrect downstream dispatches, wasted 8-min re-dispatches, and stale notification floods. Non-deterministic: ~50% reproduction rate.
aliases: Premature notification cascades to incorrect downstream dispatches
signals.review_reason: Main orchestrator flow is blocked by incorrect completion signals. Causes significant cost waste ($8-21/min additional), computation waste (re-dispatched researchers), and incorrect downstream results. The non-deterministic nature makes it especially dangerous — identical runs produce different outcomes.

source_issues.title: [Bug] TaskNotificationMessage fires while subagent is still running (premature, not cross-turn leak)
source_issues.evidence: Orchestrator dispatched 5 subagents in parallel. All 5 received premature <task-notification> while still mid-execution. Orchestrator immediately dispatched reviewers against non-existent files, then re-dispatched all 5 researchers (8 min wasted each). Actual TASK_DONE arrived 17 min later, flooding with stale notifications. Production cost impact: 32min/$21.51 vs baseline 51min/$22.33.

signals.topic: SubprocessCLITransport.close() hangs indefinitely when CLI shutdown handler blocks
signals.summary: close() sends SIGTERM to Claude Code subprocess then calls process.wait() with no timeout. If the Node.js process runs a shutdown handler that blocks (e.g., waiting for MCP server or subagent), close() blocks forever. In parallel agent runs (~200 instances), 30% of jobs hang indefinitely after successful completion, causing worker process exhaustion and VM infra timeouts.
aliases: Parallel agent worker exhaustion from hung close()
signals.review_reason: Main workflow is blocked by indefinite hang on what should be a routine cleanup call. 30% failure rate in parallel agent deployments is a high-frequency operational blocker. Causes worker process exhaustion and VM timeout cascades in production.

source_issues.title: SubprocessCLITransport.close() hangs indefinitely if subprocess shutdown handler blocks
source_issues.evidence: 30% of 200 parallel Claude Code instances via SDK hung indefinitely after job completion. Claude code finished successfully but VM stayed hanging because transport.close() never returned, causing entire worker process to hit VM infra timeout. Affects all long-running server processes that need clean shutdown.

signals.topic: stderr callback exception permanently kills _handle_stderr loop — drops all subsequent stderr lines silently
signals.summary: A single exception in the user-provided stderr callback permanently terminates the stderr processing loop via an outer try/except Exception: pass. All subsequent stderr lines for the rest of the session are silently dropped. No log, no traceback. Subsequent CLI errors that would reach the user's logger are lost forever. Silent regression with no recovery path.
aliases: Stderr callback exception permanently disables stderr piping
stderr loop silently terminated on single exception
Silent stderr drop after callback error
signals.review_reason: stderr is a critical debugging channel for SDK users. Permanently losing it after any callback error (even a transient one) means all subsequent CLI diagnostics are lost for the session. No recovery path and no warning to the user. Key observability failure in production deployments.

source_issues.title: Bug: stderr callback raise silently kills _handle_stderr loop, dropping all subsequent stderr lines
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer shows callback raising on 'line 1' causes 'line 2' to never be delivered. After first exception, all subsequent stderr is permanently lost for the session. The stderr: Callable[[str], None] | None signature does not document any 'must not raise' contract, so users have no warning.

signals.topic: TRACEPARENT / W3C trace context silently dropped on 2nd+ query() call in long-running processes
signals.summary: Bundled CLI honors TRACEPARENT only on the first query() call. On subsequent calls in the same long-running process (the dominant deployment shape per SDK hosting docs), telemetry spans become orphan roots with no parent trace. The ~/.claude/ state directory's firstStartTime marker causes OTel init to be skipped. Makes observability flows described in SDK observability docs unusable past the first call.
aliases: Telemetry trace broken after first query call
OTel span parent context lost on subsequent calls
signals.review_reason: Observability is a first-class SDK feature with documented flows. Breaking it on the 2nd+ call in every long-running process (the primary deployment shape) means all production traces beyond the first call are fragmented and unusable. Key observability pipeline failure.

source_issues.title: Bundled CLI silently drops inbound TRACEPARENT on 2nd+ query() call when ~/.claude/ has state from a prior run

signals.topic: Linux binary resolver selects wrong musl/glibc variant, causing ENOENT at spawn and blocking SDK usage on glibc systems
signals.summary: On glibc Linux (e.g. Ubuntu, GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest), the SDK's binary picker tries the musl variant first via require.resolve(). When both optional-deps are installed (common with pnpm 10), require.resolve succeeds for musl, spawn fails at execve because /lib/ld-musl-x86_64.so.1 is missing, and the error message misleadingly says 'native binary not found'. Affected users must manually specify pathToClaudeCodeExecutable as a workaround. Four distinct reports filed.
aliases: musl binary selected on glibc Linux
glibc vs musl resolver wrong order
libc variant picker failure on Linux
signals.review_reason: count=4 meets high-frequency threshold. All reports confirm the same root cause: the binary resolver in sdk.mjs tries musl before glibc on Linux, require.resolve() succeeds for the wrong variant, spawn fails with misleading ENOENT, and glibc fallback is never reached. The SDK is entirely unusable on glibc Linux systems where both optional-dep variants are installed (common with pnpm 10). This is a primary-flow block — query() throws before any Claude interaction. Multiple users require manual pathToClaudeCodeExecutable workaround, which is not documented.

signals.topic: OTel tracer emits non-semconv token attribute names, causing downstream cost tracking to fail (always $0.00)

signals.topic: Unbounded checkpoint storage growth causing disk pressure and potential data loss

signals.topic: Task retry causes duplicate tool execution — leads to duplicate payments, emails, and trades
signals.summary: When a CrewAI task fails and retries (via max_retry_limit, exception handling, or external re-trigger), any @tool decorated function that already executed successfully runs again with no idempotency guard. aliases: Idempotency guard missing on tool calls
Duplicate side effects on task retry

The LangGraph Cloud reference shows this is a systemic problem across agent frameworks. No idempotency guard exists — the framework retries successfully-executed tool calls unconditionally. This blocks production use of CrewAI with any payment/transactional external API.

signals.topic: Agent search tools scan .gemini/tmp/ causing recursive session log growth and disk/memory exhaustion

signals.review_reason: Single detailed issue with comprehensive root-cause analysis. source_issues.title: agent search tools scan .gemini/tmp/ by default, causing recursive session log growth

memory not freed after session reset

signals.review_reason: User lost active session context with no recovery path. The absence of auto-save for in-progress sessions is a data-loss issue. Users relying on the CLI for important work lose context permanently on crashes.

source_issues.title: Session loss during unexpected system shutdown

aliases: Serialization error message shows literal {e} instead of exception

signals.topic: stream_events v3: reasoning content silently dropped from AIMessage when same message contains a tool_call — breaks conversation persistence

The streamed .reasoning projection still works during the run, but the saved message loses all reasoning — invisible to users who rely on conversation history.
aliases: reasoning content lost v3 protocol tool_call
signals.review_reason: Silent data loss in a core streaming API — reasoning is visible during streaming but permanently lost from the persisted message. This breaks conversation history, replay, and audit trails for all users of Gemini (and similar) thinking-enabled models via stream_events v3. count=2 confirms this is a real, reproducible issue, not an isolated edge case. source_issues.title: stream_events(version="v3"): reasoning content dropped from AIMessage when message also contains a tool_call

It's not in content, not in additional_kwargs, not in response_metadata. Any tool-calling turn's thinking is lost from conversation history. Live SSE rendering still works; only the persisted/replayed transcript is affected.

source_issues.title: stream_events(version="v3"): reasoning content dropped from AIMessage when same message contains a tool_call
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #37420, provides root cause analysis: _finish() backfills tool_call_chunks but has no equivalent sweep for _reasoning_per_block. When a provider emits content-block-delta for reasoning but no terminating content-block-finish before message-finish, accumulated reasoning never lands in self._blocks.

signals.topic: ChatDeepSeek drops reasoning_content on outbound requests, causing API 400 errors that break multi-turn and tool-using agent flows
signals.summary: DeepSeek reasoner models require the prior turn's reasoning_content to be echoed back on each multi-turn request. ChatDeepSeek._create_chat_result captures reasoning_content from responses into additional_kwargs, but the outbound serialization path (_get_request_payload) drops it. This causes DeepSeek API to return HTTP 400 with 'reasoning_content must be passed back' on the second turn — completely breaking LangGraph create_react_agent and any multi-turn agent loop.

The API explicitly rejects the request with a 400 error. count=2 confirms this is not an isolated environment issue. source_issues.title: ChatDeepSeek drops reasoning_content on outbound requests, breaking multi-turn / tool-using flows with reasoner models

Any agent loop that follows a model response with a tool result and then re-invokes the model breaks immediately on the second turn, including create_react_agent / create_agent in LangGraph. signals.topic: grep_search Python fallback silently skips valid UTF-8 files on Windows due to read_text() encoding

aliases: python fallback utf-8 decode error windows
signals.review_reason: Windows-specific silent failure in a core search primitive. The user gets incomplete search results without any indication that files were skipped. This is a platform-specific regression that breaks the expected behavior of grep_search on Windows, a common developer OS.

source_issues.title: grep_search: Python fallback skips valid UTF-8 files on Windows due to read_text() encoding
source_issues.evidence: On Windows, the Python fallback reads files with read_text() using the process default encoding (cp1252), causing valid UTF-8 files to raise UnicodeDecodeError and be silently skipped. Searches return incomplete or empty results even when matching content exists in normal UTF-8 files.

signals.topic: SQLite checkpointer storage model causes massive DB bloat (100+ GiB) without channel normalization

Root cause is storage model parity gap between Postgres and SQLite checkpointer implementations. source_issues.title: checkpoint-sqlite: storage model does not use `new_versions` to normalize channel values like Postgres saver

signals.topic: Interrupt() inside while loop causes entire loop body to re-execute on each retry instead of resuming at correct point

The scratchpad resume counter treats loop iterations as sequential interrupt() calls instead of recognizing they belong to the same function call. This is a main workflow blocker for any LangGraph user implementing interactive forms, approval workflows, or retry logic with interrupt(). The reproduction directly follows official docs and produces visibly wrong behavior.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Interrupt() in a loop will cause extra resumes
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction follows official LangGraph docs pattern for input validation. Entering -1,-2,-3,-4,-5,-6 followed by 30 produces 21 print statements instead of 7. Each retry re-executes the entire loop body from scratch rather than resuming at the interrupt point. Root cause identified in langgraph/types.py scratchpad resume counter.

signals.topic: AsyncGraphRunStream lacks interleave() method blocking async consumption of v3 stream projections

source_issues.title: AsyncGraphRunStream lacks interleave for v3 stream projections
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction produces AttributeError: 'AsyncGraphRunStream' object has no attribute 'interleave'. Sync counterpart GraphRunStream already has interleave(). signals.topic: SyncPregelLoop.put_writes missing guard for INTERRUPT/ERROR writes causing stale error replay from cache
signals.summary: The sync path of put_writes caches task writes unconditionally including INTERRUPT/ERROR writes, whereas the async path already has this guard. With CachePolicy enabled, errors are replayed from cache instead of re-executing, bypassing retry logic.
signals.review_reason: Critical silent data corruption: errors get cached and replayed as valid results, completely bypassing retry logic. The async path is already correctly guarded, making this a clear regression in the sync path. Users with CachePolicy + sync API unknowingly get stale error state on subsequent invocations instead of retry, which can cause cascading failures in production workflows.

source_issues.title: bug: SyncPregelLoop.put_writes caches INTERRUPT/ERROR writes (async path already guarded)
source_issues.evidence: Async path already has guard at line 1407-1409 that returns early when first write is INTERRUPT or ERROR. Sync path at line 1203-1218 is missing this guard. With CachePolicy + graph.invoke() (sync), failed/interrupted node writes are cached and replayed on next invocation, silently returning stale error state.

signals.topic: addMemory Phase 1 retrieval excludes metadata from search filters causing cross-context contamination in multi-app setups

signals.topic: A2A streaming handler emits empty Parts arrays and duplicate messageId, breaking spec-compliant clients
signals.summary: A2AAgentHandler.HandleNewMessageStreamingAsync emits one A2A Message per AgentResponseUpdate chunk. Empty-content chunks (role-only, finish-only) produce Parts=[], violating the REQUIRED non-empty Parts constraint. All chunks of a single completion share the same messageId (from Responses API id), causing A2A clients to deduplicate-collapse the stream to a single empty message. Python a2a-sdk rejects these events with pydantic validation error.
aliases: A2A streaming empty Parts validation error
A2A streaming interoperability broken with Python a2a-sdk
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：A2A streaming路径对所有符合规范的客户端(特别是Python a2a-sdk)发送无效事件，消息被拒绝或被去重折叠为单条空消息。A2A是跨平台agent通信标准，streaming不可用意味着只能降级到同步路径。根因明确(workaround是禁用streaming)，严重影响跨生态互操作性。

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: A2A streaming handler emits one Message per chat-client update with shared messageId and empty Parts on bookend chunks

With validation relaxed, deduplication collapses entire stream to one (empty) message via shared messageId. Root cause in CreateMessageFromUpdate — uses update.ResponseId (shared across all chunks) and update.ToParts() returns [] for role-only/finish-only chunks. Workaround: disable streaming on agent card (loses streaming UX).

signals.topic: propagate_session=True in agent.as_tool() causes 400 BadRequest in sub-agent with Responses API (service_session_id conflict)
signals.summary: When using agent.as_tool(propagate_session=True), the child agent inherits the parent's service_session_id from the Responses API. After the parent's first LLM call, the child incorrectly sends this as previous_response_id, which the server rejects because the parent's tool_call is still pending. This causes 400 'No tool output found for function call' errors and breaks OpenTelemetry trace hierarchy.

source_issues.title: Python: propagate_session=True breaks sub-agent when using Responses API (service_session_id conflict)
source_issues.evidence: OpenAI.BadRequestError 400: 'No tool output found for function call call_yqKQ1r87I0HNWcXRxpkoqrJA'. Root cause: AgentSession conflates client-side state (session.state) with server-side conversation pointer (service_session_id). propagate_session=True passes entire session to child. After parent's first LLM call, service_session_id is auto-set, child sends it as previous_response_id, server rejects. Impact: any as_tool(propagate_session=True) fails with Responses API (MAF default). Also corrupts OpenTelemetry trace hierarchy — spans become orphaned at trace root.

signals.topic: AgentOutputSchema.name() crashes with AttributeError for Literal output types

signals.review_reason: Lack of a public .func attribute on FunctionTool blocks code-shipping SDKs and sandboxing tools at build time, and forces private __closure__ spelunking as a fragile workaround. signals.topic: Skill pipeline data injection: unsanitized external data piped into AI generation/execution contexts across 9 marketplace skills
signals.summary: Multiple skills across the ClawHub marketplace feed unsanitized external data directly into AI agent prompts, code generation pipelines, or authenticated API calls, with no instruction/data fencing, zero-width/BIDI character normalization, or output schema validation. Affected skills span Google Workspace, Sentry, GitHub, Web scraping, algorithm solving, and Supalytics — enabling credential theft, unauthorized mutations, and prompt injection.
aliases: External data injection in skill pipelines
No input sanitization in AI skill contexts
signals.review_reason: Nine separate skills all share the same architectural root cause: external data (SMS, web pages, telemetry, GitHub content, workspace files, community text, analytics fields) is ingested into the AI agent context or execution pipeline with no sanitization, no instruction/data fence, and no output normalization. Each skill also grants the agent authenticated capabilities (phone control, code execution, API mutations) that a prompt injection payload can steer. The breadth (9 skills, 5 distinct integration categories) makes this a systemic platform risk rather than isolated incidents.

signals.topic: Pre-bash hook dangerous-command validation silently passes — security gate is a no-op

signals.review_reason: Active security control (dangerous command validation) is a documented no-op for every Claude Code Bash PreToolUse call. signals.topic: Process group race: task completes before subprocess writes outputs, causing dependent builds to fail with module-not-found

Root cause is pgid-based completion tracking that has a blind spot for group-escaping descendants.
